title: Constructible exceptional adjunction and its coefficient comparisons without an ambient datum
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and the finite discrete rings $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; $X,Y$ are not required to be separated over $k$. For $\Lambda\in\{A_n,R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ use ordinary constant-$A_n$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites at finite levels, completed coefficient sheaves and derived-complete constructible objects at $R$, raw scalar localization at $E$, and common finite coefficient-field stages at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}=D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ for the full bounded constructible finite-Tor category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use compact supports $F_\Lambda=Rf_{!,\Lambda}$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and the constructible exceptional functor $G_\Lambda=Rf^!_\Lambda$ constructed by etale comparison and strict coefficient systems [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

The functors $F_\Lambda$ and $G_\Lambda$ preserve these finite-Tor categories and are exact, and there is an adjunction
$$F_\Lambda:\mathcal C_{X,\Lambda}\rightleftarrows\mathcal C_{Y,\Lambda}:G_\Lambda,\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_Y(F_\Lambda K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,G_\Lambda L),$$
natural in $K,L$. Its units $\eta_\Lambda$ and counits $\epsilon_\Lambda$ obey both triangle identities and the compactification-refinement comparisons.

For every finite extension $E\subset E'$ put $R'=\mathcal O_{E'}$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi'$ of $R'$, and put $A_{E',r}=R'/(\varpi'^r)$ for $r\ge1$; the notation $\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda'}$, $F_{\Lambda'}$ and $G_{\Lambda'}$ at these target coefficient stages uses the same constructions with $E'$ in place of $E$. Finite coefficient change means derived extension of scalars along the displayed map of constant ring sheaves, integral reduction is [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], integral scalar extension is [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and rational scalar extension and rationalization are [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].

For each coefficient change $T_T:\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda}\to\mathcal C_{T,\Lambda'}$ given by a finite quotient $A_n\to A_m$ ($1\le m\le n$), integral reduction $R\to A_n$, finite-level scalar extension $A_n\to B_n=\mathcal O_{E'}/\varpi^n\mathcal O_{E'}$ for a finite extension $E\subset E'$ and any further coefficient quotient, integral or rational scalar extension along such an extension, or rationalization $R\to E$, the canonical comparisons
$$q:T_YF_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\Lambda'}T_X,\qquad b:T_XG_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{\Lambda'}T_Y$$
are isomorphisms on the stated domains and satisfy, with the components evaluated at the indicated objects,
$$G_{\Lambda'}(q_K)\circ b_{F_\Lambda K}\circ T_X(\eta_{\Lambda,K})=\eta_{\Lambda',T_XK},$$
$$\epsilon_{\Lambda',T_YL}\circ F_{\Lambda'}(b_L)\circ q_{G_\Lambda L}=T_Y(\epsilon_{\Lambda,L}).$$
For the finite-level scalar change, if $e=e(E'/E)$ and $\varpi'$ is a uniformizer of $\mathcal O_{E'}$, then $(\varpi^n)=(\varpi'^{en})$, so $B_n$ is the coefficient ring $A_{E',en}$; any further quotient is to $A_{E',m}$ with $1\le m\le en$. These comparisons satisfy the identity and composition cocycles, commute with shifts, and define the corresponding comparisons in the common-stage category. For field coefficients finite reduction refers to chosen integral representatives before rationalization, not to a reduction functor on the field category. No right adjoint on an unrestricted pro-etale ambient category is asserted.

source.place: Paragraphs defining the constructible exceptional functor, its higher coefficient stages and the natural adjunction isomorphisms; theorem obligations explicitly distinguished from the optional ambient datum.

proof.text: Work first at a fixed finite coefficient stage and a fixed compactification $c=(j,p_f)$. The scheme $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$: cover $Y$ by finitely many affine charts whose coordinate algebras have finite sets of $k$-algebra generators, and cover the preimages by finitely many affine charts with finitely generated algebras over those coordinate rings (the proper morphism $p_f$ is of finite type). The images of the base generators together with the relative generators generate each source algebra over $k$, giving a finite affine cover of finite type. Choose a nonnegative integer $d$ bounding its dimension, using lem-kun-dimension-finite-type (take $d=0$ for an empty scheme). The open extension theorem puts $j_!K$ in the finite-Tor category with the original Tor interval $[a,b]$; apply cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale to the proper morphism $p_f$ to obtain $F_AK=Rp_{f,*}j_!K$ constructible with Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$. All these schemes are Noetherian by the finite-type-over-Noetherian theorem. The bound is independent of the finite coefficient exponent. Exact open extension and derived direct image are triangulated, so this restriction of $F_A$ is exact.

source.place: Construction 2.17, Theorem 2.18; finite-coefficient constructibility and uniform bounds, with the cited DAG statements supplying the precise pro-etale conclusions.

proof.text: Apply cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum to $f$ itself. Its hypotheses allow $X$ and $Y$ to be nonseparated over $k$. It gives bounded constructible and finite-Tor preservation for $G_A$, with constants depending on a finite family of affine presentations of $f$, independent of the coefficient exponent. Every bounded constructible input is of etale origin by lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin. Consequently the natural Hom bijection of thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class applies to every $K,L$ in the two finite-Tor categories. These are full triangulated subcategories by lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated. Restrict that bijection and use lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection: $\eta_K$ is the transpose of $1_{F_AK}$ and $\epsilon_L$ the inverse transpose of $1_{G_AL}$, and both triangles hold. Equip the right adjoint with the shift comparison obtained by transposing the shift comparison of $F_A$: its unit and counit commute with shifts by the two transpose formulas, and lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint makes $G_A$ exact. This is the transported etale adjunction; it makes no assertion about a right adjoint to compact supports on unrestricted pro-etale objects.

source.place: Propositions 2.23, 2.29(2), 3.16(2); current blueprint exceptional-functor paragraph, constructible typing and adjunction. The local smooth-purity prerequisite is the existing lecture-notes route of cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum.

proof.text: The finite scalar-change functors have the asserted domains even for a nonflat quotient. Indeed a finite-Tor input has a bounded flat model by lem-sf-flat-model. After extension from $A$ to the finite ring $B$, each term is $B$-flat: tensoring it with a $B$-module is the original flat term tensored with the underlying $A$-module. Thus the same interval is a Tor bound. Cohomological constructibility of the tensor with the constant finite $A$-module $B$ follows from lem-pur-finite-tensor-constructible-cohomology. This also gives constructibility as a $B$-module: on each locally constant finite $A$-stratum, the finitely many endomorphisms giving the $B$-action are locally constant after refining the trivializing etale covers, so the same sheaf is locally constant with finite $B$-stalk. This applies to $A_n\to A_m$, to $A_n\to R'/\varpi^nR'$, and to their composites. No flatness of $A_m$ over $A_n$ is used.

source.place: Finite-coefficient change of rings; Proposition 2.29(2). Constructibility input is Stacks Tag 09BQ (proetale.tex, lemma-tensor-c).

proof.text: Prove finite coefficient comparisons on the ordinary etale derived categories before restricting them. Write $F_A^e\dashv G_A^e$ for ordinary etale compact support and its right adjoint. For $A\to B$ as in step 3, restriction $r_T$ from $B$ to $A$ is exact and reflects isomorphisms, since its cohomology is the same underlying sheaf. There is a canonical identification $r_YF_B^e\cong F_A^e r_X$: open extension commutes with restriction termwise, and the proper-direct-image identification is the two factorizations of the same ringed-topos morphism in lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition. For the identity topos morphism with structural ring map A to B, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction gives the underived extension/restriction adjunction. Its left derived functor is everywhere defined by lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings; restriction is exact, so its termwise functor is its absolute right derived functor. Lemma lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived therefore supplies the derived extension/restriction adjunction on these ordinary etale categories. Apply lem-pur-etale-exceptional-constant-tensor with the constant complex $V=B\in D(A\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$. Its first tensor comparison, read using $r_YF_B^e\cong F_A^e r_X$, proves that the specified $q:T_YF_A^e\to F_B^eT_X$ is an isomorphism. Adjunction then identifies $r_XG_B^e$ with $G_A^e r_Y$: for every $H$, the chain $\operatorname{Hom}_A(H,r_XG_B^eM)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(T_XH,G_B^eM)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(F_B^eT_XH,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(F_A^eH,r_YM)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(H,G_A^e r_YM)$ is natural, using $q$ in the middle. Under this identification, restriction of the counit-transpose $b:T_XG_A^e\to G_B^eT_Y$ is exactly the second tensor comparison in lem-pur-etale-exceptional-constant-tensor, as its displayed transpose shows. That comparison is invertible for $V=B$ even when $B$ is not perfect over $A$; conservativity of $r_X$ proves $b$ invertible. The ordinary etale right adjoints used here exist by thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint; no separatedness of the schemes over $k$ enters this argument.

source.place: Construction 2.26 and Proposition 2.29(2), constant coefficient complex B; Stacks Tag 0D6E for ringed-topos derived composition.

proof.text:
Transport step 4 to the finite constructible pro-etale categories. Use the etale-origin equivalence of lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin and its Tor-amplitude equivalence lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude, and use thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison to identify $R
u_*
u^*$ with the identity on bounded-below etale complexes. The compact-support identification is the named comparison of lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison; the exceptional identification is $
u_X^*G_A^eR
u_{Y,*}$ from step 2. Exact inverse image commutes with tensor of constant coefficients: on a flat resolution this is the balancing map $
u^*(P\otimes_A B)\cong
u^*P\otimes_A B$. Therefore the transported $q$ is the canonical compact-support coefficient map, and $b$ is its counit-normalized transpose. Units and counits here are exactly those in step 2, since both were obtained from the same natural Hom bijection. The simultaneous section models of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections apply to the inverse images, derived direct images, open extension, coefficient tensor and their transposes. Thus these are coherent maps of coefficient systems, rather than choices of maps inferred from finite objectwise isomorphisms.

source.place: Finite etale/pro-etale comparison in the current exceptional-functor definition; Construction 5.15 and Lemma 5.16 for simultaneous coefficient systems.

proof.text: At each coefficient change define $b_L$ as the $F'\dashv G'$ transpose of $T_Y\epsilon_L\circ q_{G L}^{-1}$. The inverse-transpose formula gives $\epsilon'_{T_YL}\circ F'(b_L)\circ q_{G L}=T_Y\epsilon_L$, the requested counit equation. For the unit equation compare $b_{F K}\circ T_X\eta_K$ and $G'(q_K^{-1})\circ\eta'_{T_XK}$ as maps $T_XK\to G'T_YF K$. Their $F'\dashv G'$ inverse transposes are both $q_K^{-1}$: for the first, naturality of $q$ reduces the transpose to $T_Y(\epsilon_{F K}\circ F\eta_K)\circ q_K^{-1}=q_K^{-1}$ by the first triangle; for the second this is the unit-transpose formula. Injectivity of transposition proves equality; composing with $G'(q_K)$ gives the displayed unit equation. Identity and composition for $q$ are the coherent tensor comparisons of step 5, and identity and composition for $b$ follow by mate pasting. This proves the mixed finite-quotient/finite-extension cocycles, including the equations on units and counits.

source.place: Adjunction transposes and pasting, Stacks Tag 0037 and the mate-pasting formulas; explicit calculation from the finite comparisons.

proof.text: Assemble the finite functors as functors of normalized derived coefficient systems. On the full stable enhanced finite-Tor subcategories take the enhanced $F_n$ supplied by lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections, and the equivalences $q$ and ordinary adjoints $G_n$ of steps 1--6. The finite-Tor categories are stable by lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated. All hypotheses of lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates now hold, including invertibility of the right mates. It produces enhanced right-adjoint realizations and an adjunction $\mathcal F\dashv\mathcal G$ on cartesian sections, with actual coherent unit/counit maps and their triangle identities. Semilinear-derived-sections identifies these sections with normalized strict derived systems. This realization of $\mathcal G$ is the one in def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image: the system adjoint of lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint is first transported by the system site comparison of lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison. On bounded-below systems with etale-origin evaluations the system counit is an isomorphism, so the same Hom chain as the finite comparison transports the system adjunction. Its evaluations and counits are the finite ones; uniqueness of the right adjoint identifies it with the section realization, as a natural isomorphism of system functors compatible with the adjunction, not just a list of identifications of evaluated objects.

source.place: Constructions 5.14--5.15, Lemmas 5.16 and 5.22, Proposition 5.24; the cited general cartesian-section lemma supplies enhanced adjunction descent.

proof.text: Use the reduction/limit adjunction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$ of lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus. Its unit is invertible on the derived-complete objects in question: compute it from the strict augmentation $P\to(P\otimes A_n)_n$, $x\mapsto(x\otimes1)_n$, on one K-flat representative and then apply total limit. In the Roos cone model this is the augmentation into the product with zero shifted-product component, exactly the specified construction of $\chi_{E/E}$ in lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison after $P\otimes_RR=P$. This identifies the actual unit using its complex model, rather than only its projections. The $E'=E$ case of lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison explicitly asserts that this same natural map is an isomorphism on derived-complete objects. Its counit is invertible on normalized systems by lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity, with the canonical coherent counit comparisons of that statement. Thus reduction and total limit give inverse equivalences between the integral finite-Tor category and normalized systems with bounded constructible finite-Tor evaluations having common cohomological and Tor bounds. For the reverse direction, effectivity gives derived completeness and the prescribed reductions; the common bounds are exactly the two integral definitions. The equivalence is fully faithful on morphisms because it is an adjunction with invertible unit and counit. This use of strict derived systems avoids inferring equality of integral maps merely from equality of their reductions.

source.place: Coefficient completion and normalization; compare Bhatt--Scholze Definitions 3.5.2, 6.8.1 and Lemma 6.8.2; the general system adjunction/effectivity nodes specify the canonical maps.

proof.text: The system functors in step 7 preserve the common bounds needed in step 8. For $\mathcal F$, step 1 gives the same Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$ at every finite level. Taking the degree-zero test module $A_n$ in the definition of Tor amplitude shows that these same intervals bound cohomology, since $F_{A_n}K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_n\cong F_{A_n}K_n$. Thus the cohomological bound is uniform as well. Lemma lem-coef-integral-compact-support identifies its total limit, with its finite projections, with the integral $Rf_!$ of the item. For $\mathcal G$, cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum gives common cohomological and Tor intervals independent of $n$; normalization of its strict realization is also stated in lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint and preserved by system comparison. Effectivity therefore puts its total limit in the integral finite-Tor category, and this limit is precisely the integral $Rf^!$ in the definition. Conjugate the system adjunction by the equivalences of step 8: $\operatorname{Hom}(F_RK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal R_YL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal G\mathcal R_YL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,G_RL)$. This is natural, so its units, counits and triangles are the transported system ones. Evaluation gives the integral-reduction comparisons and both equations of step 6 as actual maps of systems. Exactness follows from the exact finite system functors and the exact total-limit functor of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, restricted to the full triangulated integral finite-Tor categories.

source.place: Lemma 5.22, Proposition 5.24 and Construction 5.25 (printed pp. 36--37), with the integral equivalence and uniform finite-Tor bounds established in steps 8--9.

proof.text: For $E\subset E'$, use the finite-free system comparison of lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint, transported as in step 7; the compact-support system comparison is the coherent $q$ of steps 4--5. The former statement includes identity, composition, quotient compatibility and agreement on the subsequence $B_n=R'/\varpi^nR'=R'/\varpi'^{en}R'$. On normalized systems this subsequence loses no data: recover level $m$ by choosing $n$ with $en\geq m$ and taking the derived quotient of level $en$ to $m$; the normalization cocycle identifies the results for two choices of $n$. This also specifies morphisms and inverse comparisons, so gives an equivalence of the normalized section categories. Under the completion equivalence, the resulting scalar functor is the integral scalar extension in the item: lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison identifies that strict-tower functor with ordinary tensor by the finite-free completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R'_T$. Its derived reductions are the same $B_n$ tensors, by associativity, and it is derived complete. Constructibility is stated in lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible, and the flat-model argument of step 3 gives a common Tor interval. Conjugate the coherent system $q,b$ and the system unit/counit equations through these equivalences. This produces integral scalar comparison isomorphisms and the stated equations, with their quotient, identity and composition coherences. All identifications here are of functors and system maps before total limit; no faithfulness of reduction on individual ordinary derived-category Hom groups is assumed.

source.place: Finite-free system comparison and normalization; cofinal powers of uniformizers in the current exceptional-functor construction.

proof.text: Pass to $E$ by the raw scalar localization in def-weil-rationalization-karoubi. Every integral constructible object lies in the integral finite-Tor category by lem-coef-integral-residue-tor, so step 9 is available on every integral representative of a rational object. The integral functors, comparisons and adjunction are $R$-linear: their complex and coefficient-system constructions commute with scalar multiplication; equivalently their adjunction transposes satisfy $\Psi(ah)=a\Psi(h)$. Tensor each Hom bijection with $E$ and its inverse with $E$. They remain inverse and natural, giving $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(F_EK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,G_EL)$. Units, counits and all their equations are the images of the integral ones, since they are defined by the images of identities. The definitions give $q,b$ for rationalization itself, and localizing step 10 gives the comparisons for finite rational scalar extensions. A distinguished rational triangle is isomorphic to an integral triangle's image, so the localized functors are exact by the scalar-localization triangulation theorem. No idempotent completion is inserted.

source.place: Raw scalar localization and passage of operations, Zheng Section 6; explicit Hom-module localization argument following the current coefficient definitions.

proof.text: Finally use the common-stage definition of def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients. For $K$ represented over $E$ and $L$ over $E'$, choose a common finite coefficient field $H$; step 11 gives a Hom bijection there. For a further finite extension write $T$ for scalar extension and $\Psi,\Psi'$ for the two adjunction bijections. If $h:F K\to L$, its scalar extension has source identified by $q_K$, so its representative is $T_Yh\circ q_K^{-1}$. Naturality of $b$ and the unit equation give $\Psi'(T_Yh\circ q_K^{-1})=G'(T_Yh)\circ G'(q_K^{-1})\circ\eta'_{T_XK}=G'(T_Yh)\circ b_{F K}\circ T_X\eta_K=b_L\circ T_X(\Psi(h))$. Thus the bijections commute with the transition maps on both Hom groups. Their inverses commute too, by applying the inverse bijection to this equality. Taking the directed colimit of these bijections and their inverses therefore gives inverse natural maps on the displayed common-stage Hom groups. Objects, maps, units and counits are represented at a common finite stage; the triangle and coefficient-composition equations hold there, hence also in the common-stage category. Every distinguished triangle is represented at a finite stage, proving exactness. This defines the functors and comparisons independently of representatives. Finite reduction at a field stage is interpreted only after choosing its integral representative, as required in the statement.

source.place: Common finite coefficient-field stages, final higher-coefficient paragraphs of the exceptional-functor definition.

proof.text: The remaining refinement and shift normalizations hold simultaneously with the coefficient comparisons. At finite levels thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class states compactification-cocycle compatibility of the Hom bijections, and prop-compactification-coherence-detailed identifies the compact-support maps. For a refinement write $a:F_1\xrightarrow{\sim}F_2$ for that comparison, and define $\rho_L:G_2L\to G_1L$ as the $F_1\dashv G_1$ transpose of $\epsilon_{2,L}\circ a_{G_2L}$. Then $\epsilon_{1,L}\circ F_1(\rho_L)=\epsilon_{2,L}\circ a_{G_2L}$ by inverse transposition. The inverse transposes of $\rho_{F_2K}\circ\eta_{2,K}$ and $G_1(a_K)\circ\eta_{1,K}$ both equal $a_K$: for the first use the preceding counit identity, naturality of $a$, and $\epsilon_{2,F_2K}\circ F_2\eta_{2,K}=1$; for the second use the unit-transpose formula. Hence these two maps agree. Transposing $a^{-1}$ gives the inverse of $\rho$, and mate pasting proves identity, composition and compatibility with the coherent coefficient squares. These formulas establish refinement compatibility of both adjunction maps. Lemma lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections realizes these maps and their compositions on systems, so step 7, the completion equivalence and scalar localization carry the same identities to the higher stages. For shifts, the finite $F$ is the usual derived exact functor, and the shift of $G$ is its adjunction-compatible shift from step 2. Tensor, comparison and normalized system maps commute with shifts on the complex models; the formula $b_L=G'(T_Y\epsilon_L\circ q_{G L}^{-1})\circ\eta'_{T_XG L}$ therefore identifies its shifted value with the shifted $b_L$, using shift compatibility of each factor. Total limit is exact, and scalar localization and common-stage shifts are defined stagewise, so these shift identities persist. Empty $X$ gives zero functors and unique comparisons. If $Y$ is empty, so is $X$; use zero bounds rather than a dimension or a maximum of empty charts. Identity coefficient changes, including $n=m$, give identities by step 6, and ramified extensions use $en$, never an unadjusted $n$.

No statement change, no new nodes.
